text:
maria: Quick preflight — ACME is asking for a private/VPC pod sizing for their Q4 holiday peak (Black Friday -> Cyber Monday window). They expect up to 4x baseline traffic. I started a rough burn-rate + GPU-hours calc, can folks sanity-check?

ajay: Thanks. Share the baseline numbers you used? qps baseline, avg tokens per request, model choice?

maria: Baseline: 250 qps sustained (weekday), average prompt+response ~ 300 tokens, model = quantized Llama2-70B variant we plan to serve. Target headroom = 4x for peak bursts, 99th latency SLO 250ms. Region: eu-west-1 (customer legal constraint).

chris: Note EU region has a smaller spare pool in our current fleet (limited A100 availability). If they want physical on-prem pod we need to consider 8–12 week procurement lead time for A100s.

hailey: Also add network egress constraints — their VPC egress goes through a single NAT; need to size throughput. For 1000 qps (4x), 1000 * 300 tokens/request * avg 4 bytes/token ~ 1.2MB/s ~ 86Mbps just for model IO (rough). Add telemetry+logs ~ +30% overhead.

maria: I mocked a quick calc (posting raw so we can iterate):
```
# assumptions
baseline_qps = 250
peak_multiplier = 4
peak_qps = baseline_qps * peak_multiplier  # 1000 qps
avg_tokens = 300
requests_per_hour = peak_qps * 3600  # 3.6M req/hr
tokens_per_hour = requests_per_hour * avg_tokens  # 1.08B tokens/hr
# estimate tokens a single GPU can produce per hour (quantized, continuous-batching)
gpu_tokens_per_hour = 36_000_000  # conservative for our runtime on A100 80GB
nodes_needed = ceil(tokens_per_hour / gpu_tokens_per_hour)  # => ~30 nodes
# GPU-hours for a 72-hour Black Friday weekend (72hr)
total_gpu_hours = nodes_needed * 72
```

ajay: Those numbers look plausible. For 1.08B tokens/hr / 36M = 30 GPUs. I'd recommend adding 20% spare for network/concurrency => 36 GPUs. So total GPU-hours = 36 * 72 = 2592 GPU-hours for the weekend.

luis: From finance side — run-rate cost estimate: if committed A100 cost ~ $3.25/hr (blended), weekend cost ~ 2592 * 3.25 = $8,424. Add storage and bandwidth ~ +$1k. For a dedicated on-prem quote, capex will dwarf that but monthly op cost roughly equivalent.

ken: Action item: Maria to confirm if customer needs dedicated racks (on-prem) vs. private VPC in our coloc. That changes procurement.

maria: Confirmed: customer asked for "customer-managed hardware or Redwood-managed private pod (colocated)" options. They want both quotes.

hailey: For private/collocated option, we should recommend a 40-GPU pod (A100 80GB or equivalent). Rationale: 36 required + 10% for failover + 10% for scheduled maintenance/rollouts => ~40. Also network NICs: 100Gbps aggregated, minimum 2x 100Gb NICs per rack.

chris: If they prefer newer Hopper or H100-equivalent, we'll re-run perf numbers (H100 may increase gpu_tokens_per_hour to ~55M) — that would drop nodes to ~20. But H100 procurement is even longer and more expensive. Document both options in the quote.

maria: I've got a short checklist for the sizing doc I plan to hand to sales: 1) baseline inputs (qps, tokens, model variant) 2) perf assumption (gpu_tokens_per_hour) 3) headroom policy (x1.2 spare) 4) network I/O sizing 5) procurement lead times & capex vs opex comparison 6) suggested pod config + NICs + rack power 7) fallback plan (fallback to smaller model, burst routing to hosted) 8) estimated weekend GPU-hours + cost.

sre-bot: reminder: create a capacity ticket for procurement if nodes_needed >= 30.

ajay: I'll take perf sim run with both A100 and H100 numbers and add a sensitivity table (tokens/hr vs GPUs needed). Expect results in ~24hrs.

maria: Great — please also include a worst-case cold-start impact (KV cache warmup adds ~15–25% latency and increases token burn in first 4 hours). We'll recommend warm-up traffic and preloading.

luis: I'll draft the cost appendix for both OPEX (colocated managed pod) and CAPEX (customer buys hardware) with 3-year TCO.

ken: Once Ajay + Luis have their numbers, let's sync and produce a single-page sizing recommendation + one-page quote for Sales. Aim to have this to Sales by EOD Friday.

maria: Perfect — thanks everyone. I'll post the draft doc in #eng-platform for review later today. :thumbsup:
